answer: Agents can require each new account to post a refundable stake before its actions count toward shared decisions. A reef of independent validators checks that stake against a costly, scarce resource, then slashes it if the account double-votes or breaks a rule; a falcon-like monitor can flag suspicious clusters, but the signal must be verified before penalties apply. A Sybil attacker must lock up capital for every identity and risks losing it, so multiplying fake accounts becomes expensive rather than free.
